Day treach gra
DR JUSTICE DIY CHANDRACHUD
Judge, Supreme Court of India
Foreword
The e-Committee of the Supreme Court has been at the forefront of introducing
digital reforms in the field of law. In the past one year, the pandemic has also pushed
advocates, judges and litigants to adopt high tech solutions due to the closure of
offices and courts in light of lockdowns and public health concerns. Working
remotely, virtual courts, digital workplaces and electronic case management have
become integral to how the legal profession is practiced and conducted. This has
given us a rare opportunity to embrace technology not just as an interim measure but
to transform our legal system to make it more efficient, inclusive, accessible and
environmentally sustainable. The e-Courts Services Mobile Application is a step in
this direction.
The e-Courts Services Mobile Application is a one stop electronic case management
tool (ECT) for advocates and litigants for cases filed in the District Courts and High
Courts. It provides complete case history from filing till disposal including date wise
case diary. It allows users to access orders/judgments, cause list, transfer details of
the case and interim application status. A unique feature of the application is that an
advocate can maintain a digital diary of all cases under "My Cases" tab.
All these facilities are available free of cost. The usage of the application will not only
reduce the footfall at the court complexes but will also save time and effort for
judges, court staff and other stakeholders. It will also ensure that geographical

we crite
DR JUSTICE DY CHANDRACHUD
Judge, Supreme Court of India
constraints do not hinder access to relevant case information. We have also attempted to make the
application accessible to persons with disabilities.
The ECT tools have been discussed in detail in the manual with screenshots. Keeping in mind the
linguistic and cultural diversity of India, the manual has been translated in 11 regional languages.
The improvement in technological capacities must be accompanied by a change in culture and
mindset. I am happy to note that many advocates and litigants have already embraced the services
offered through this mobile application with more than 57 lakh downloads so far. The application will
pave the way for optimizing our legal system in an ever-evolving digital world.
[Dr Justice D Y Chandrachud]

BARUN MITRA, IAS
THE МАНАТИА
SECRETARY
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
FOREWORD
As the legal world is gradually turning digital globally, the process of ICT
enablement of the judicial landscape in India has concurrently made significant
strides. As an integral part of this multi-dimensional initiative, the eCourts
Services Mobile App has been widely hailed as an effective Electronic Case
Management Tool (ECT). Its popularity is manifested in the growing number
of downloads by lawyers, having already crossed the 57 lakh figure.
Robust Case Management and sound supporting systems are at the
core of any well-functioning legal architecture. ECT tool, enables a lawyer to
efficiently manage case information, document assembly, calendaring, time-
tracking of case status, accessing judicial decisions, compliance requirements
etc. To cap it, ECT is of immense convenience being available 24 × 7 with no
geographical boundaries and easy access on no-cost basis. The eCourts
Services Mobile App with its digital diary features has thus evolved into a
must-have tool for lawyers to promotetheir professional efficiency.
Publication of this Manual on eCourts Services Mobile App is yet
another laudable step by the Committee of the Supreme Court to create large
scale awareness of this ECT and in bringing its benefits to the doorstep of
the lawyers' community. The manual is also available in Hindi and several
other regional languages like Punjabi, Tamil, Gujarati, Odia and Nepali thus
enhancing its outreach. I am confident that this Manual will be of great utility
for the legal fraternity.
25th February, 2021
New Delhi
(Barun Mitra)

DR JUSTICE DIY CHANDRACHUD
Judge, Supreme Court of India
Foreword
The e-Committee of the Supreme Court has been at the forefront of introducing
digital reforms in the field of law. In the past one year, the pandemic has also pushed
advocates, judges and litigants to adopt high tech solutions due to the closure of
offices and courts in light of lockdowns and public health concerns. Working
remotely, virtual courts, digital workplaces and electronic case management have
become integral to how the legal profession is practiced and conducted. This has
given us a rare opportunity to embrace technology not just as an interim measure but
to transform our legal system to make it more efficient, inclusive, accessible and
environmentally sustainable. The e-Courts Services Mobile Application is a step in
this direction.
The e-Courts Services Mobile Application is a one stop electronic case management
tool (ECT) for advocates and litigants for cases filed in the District Courts and High
Courts. It provides complete case history from filing till disposal including date wise
case diary. It allows users to access orders/judgments, cause list, transfer details of
the case and interim application status. A unique feature of the application is that an
advocate can maintain a digital diary of all cases under "My Cases" tab.
All these facilities are available free of cost. The usage of the application will not only
reduce the footfall at the court complexes but will also save time and effort for
judges, court staff and other stakeholders. It will also ensure that geographical

we crite

Judge, Supreme Court of India
constraints do not hinder access to relevant case information. We have also attempted to make the
application accessible to persons with disabilities.
The ECT tools have been discussed in detail in the manual with screenshots. Keeping in mind the
linguistic and cultural diversity of India, the manual has been translated in 11 regional languages.
The improvement in technological capacities must be accompanied by a change in culture and
mindset. I am happy to note that many advocates and litigants have already embraced the services
offered through this mobile application with more than 57 lakh downloads so far. The application will
pave the way for optimizing our legal system in an ever-evolving digital world.
[Dr Justice D Y Chandrachud]

BARUN MITRA, IAS
THE МАНАТИА
SECRETARY
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
FOREWORD
As the legal world is gradually turning digital globally, the process of ICT
enablement of the judicial landscape in India has concurrently made significant
strides. As an integral part of this multi-dimensional initiative, the eCourts
Services Mobile App has been widely hailed as an effective Electronic Case
Management Tool (ECT). Its popularity is manifested in the growing number
of downloads by lawyers, having already crossed the 57 lakh figure.
Robust Case Management and sound supporting systems are at the
core of any well-functioning legal architecture. ECT tool, enables a lawyer to
efficiently manage case information, document assembly, calendaring, time-
tracking of case status, accessing judicial decisions, compliance requirements
etc. To cap it, ECT is of immense convenience being available 24 × 7 with no
geographical boundaries and easy access on no-cost basis. The eCourts
Services Mobile App with its digital diary features has thus evolved into a
must-have tool for lawyers to promotetheir professional efficiency.
Publication of this Manual on eCourts Services Mobile App is yet
another laudable step by the Committee of the Supreme Court to create large
scale awareness of this ECT and in bringing its benefits to the doorstep of
the lawyers' community. The manual is also available in Hindi and several
other regional languages like Punjabi, Tamil, Gujarati, Odia and Nepali thus
enhancing its outreach. I am confident that this Manual will be of great utility
for the legal fraternity.
25th February, 2021
New Delhi
(Barun Mitra)

iv e-Courts Services Mobile App

“e-Courts Services” Mobile Application.
1.Introduction:
Have you ever dreamt of having all your case status in your hands that too
24*7? The dream has come true with the e-Courts services mobile App. Now
anyone can access the case status, court orders, cause list through their mobile
phone without physically going to the concerned court complex. e-Committee,
Supreme Court of India released a mobile application in the name "e-Courts
Services" for the benefit of the Litigants, Lawyers, law firms, Police, Government
Agencies and other Institutional Litigants.
The mobile application comes with options like the searching case with CNR
number, searching case status using case number, Filing number, Party Names, FIR
number, Advocate details, Acts, case type. You can also view the Case History,
Diary of a case, Cause list, transfer details of the case, Order and Judgment all free
of cost through the e-Courts mobile App. You can download it from the Google
play store like any other app for android phones and the Apple app store for
iPhone, iPad devices. The download link provided on the official e-
Committee website https://ecommitteesci.gov.in & eCourts services
website https://ecourts.gov.in from where you can also download.
All the e-Courts services are available under the e-Courts mobile App, with
one added advantage in the e-Courts mobile App that it can be customized using
the My cases option available in it, which is equivalent to a digital diary for an
advocate/ litigant. Using 'My Cases', one can add the personal case numbers and
can get automatic updates. It is also helpful for litigants, firms, companies or
organization having multiple cases in different Courts at different places. In 'My
Cases', one can add his personalized list of cases and get all updates through the
e-Courts mobile application. The e-Courts Services mobile App is no doubt your
personalized digital case diary with all the case details available in your hands (set)
24*7 free of cost.
Page no 1 e-Courts Services Mobile App

1.2.Download from https://ecommitteesci.gov.in & https://ecourts.gov.in

If you have an android smartphone, search the Google Play Store for e-Courts
Services mobile app and click download and then after download, click Install,
then the mobile App is installed in your android smartphone.
1.4. Download directly from the Apple Store for iPhone/iPad:

app" and click download and then after download, click Install. Then the mobile
App is installed on your Apple iPhone. Similarly, for iPad e-Courts Services mobile
App is available, which can be downloaded and installed on iPad.

The current version of the e-Courts mobile App provides services under three

District Court or High Court or Both. For that, you need to select the Configure
option from the menu list by clicking on the icon. You can configure your mobile

6. Search cases option:
Under the e-Courts mobile App, there are two main search menus
(I) CNR search; (ii) Case Status (search); Let us see one by one hereunder.
7.Search Cases Using CNR Number:
Search by CNR number is the quickest way to get case details in
your phone using the mobile App. Do you want to know what is CNR
number, then kindly keep reading.
7.1.What is CNR number:
The CNR means Case Number Record. CNR is a unique 16 digit number given to all
cases. To put it in short, it is the unique case identity number by which any Case
can be identified. CNR is assigned to each Case filed through Case Information
System. It’s just like the PNR number used in train tickets. Anyone can trace his Case
at High Court and District Court with CNR number, which is unique 16 digit CNR
number.
CNR (16 digits) contains (State code) (District code) (Establishment code)
(Case filing number)(Filing year) Eg (JK) (AN) (01) (000638) (2017)
Example of CNR
number from various states
(I) Punjab,
(ii) Meghalaya,
(iii) Tamil Nadu
are given herewith for
clear under-standing.
Page no 10 e-Courts Services Mobile App

7.2. How to know Your CNR number:
A litigant /advocate or anyone can get the CNR for every Case in two ways
(I)From the e-Courts Services mobile App; (ii) From the e-Courts service’s website
link.
7.3.How to Get the CNR number from the e-Courts mobile App:
To get the CNR number, you should have the particulars of District, Court name
and anyone particular like Case number or Filing number or Name of Parties etc.
Let us see step by step process how to get the CNR number from the e-Courts
mobile App using the case number. Example: How to find the CNR number for OS
50/2017 of Sub court, Avinashi, Tiruppur District, Tamil Nadu.

# eCourts Services Mobile Application: Operational Guide
## Downloading Judgments, Court Orders & Business Calendar

8.9 Pre-Trial Application
This option will be the most used and very satisfying in the mobile App. The
introductory option did not have this option. But there were so many demands
whether we could get the bail, remand status under the mobile App. And now the
latest version has been updated with this helpful option of searching the Pre-Trail
applications like remand, bail etc. Just visualize you could get the remand
details/bail order in the click of a mouse in your handset. It is a tempting option; just
try it on your mobile phone.
8.9.1.How to know the bail status:
How to know the bail status:
→ Click Case Status
→ Select State, District
→click Pre trial option
→ select court complex
→ Select Police Station
→Enter FIR number& year
→Select radio button – Bail
-→Click go
-→Click the Total number of cases
-→It displays the bail details
Page no 22 e-Courts Services Mobile App

8.9.2. How to know the remand status:
Suppose any person is taken to custody and wanted to know whether he is
remanded or not which is a very sensitive search for the family or advocate of the
person concerned; in that case, they can check the remand status using the FIR
number. Example: whether any person remanded under the FIR number 2672020 of
a particular police station. Then this option comes in handy, and follow the step to
find out the remand status as shown hereunder. The remand result will be shown
with the type of remands i.e PCR Police custody remand; MCR Magisterial custody
remand.
How to know the remand status:
→Click Case Status
→ Select State, District-
→click Pre-trial option
→ select court complex
→Select Police Station
→Enter FIR number& year
→Select the radio button for remand
→click go
→Click the Total number of cases
→It displays the remand details
Page no 23 e-Courts Services Mobile App

8.9.3. How to know the Pre-Trial- Application status
In a theft case, if the property is recovered and the owner of the property files the
application for interim custody of the property at the Pre-Trial stage, then that type
of Pre-trial application status can also be checked under this option. Follow the
step to find out the pre-trial application status as shown hereunder
How to know the
Pre-Trial application status:
→ Click Case Status
→ Select State, District
→Click Pre-Trial option
→ Select Court Complex
→ Select Police Station
→Enter FIR Number
→Enter the year
→Select radio button- Application
→Click Go
→Click the Total number of cases
→It displays the Application Status
Page no 24 e-Courts Services Mobile App

9.Getting Cause list through e-Courts Mobile App:
Getting a Cause list in the mobile App is an equally useful option for Advocates,
Litigants and Judges. Three types of cause list (i) Civil Cause list of any Court (ii)
Criminal cause list of any Court (iii) Advocate wise cause list, all can be generated
under the e-Courts mobile App.
The civil cause list and the criminal cause list can be viewed under this "Cause list"
option. The Advocate wise Cause list can be viewed through the Advocate option
available under the Case Status search, which is explained under the topic "Search
using Case Status option". By using the cause list option, one can confirm whether
his case is posted on a particular day or not. It is a valuable time management tool
for Judges, staffs, Advocates through which one can find out how many cases are
listed on any specific day and the day's work can be planned, and this data can
now be viewed through the mobile App in the handsets.
1 Click Cause List icon.
2 Select State, District.
3 Select Court Complex
4 Select Court Name
5 Select Cause List Date
from the Calendar
6 Click Civil or Criminal,
Then the Cause list
civil/criminal is displayed
7 Using the search box
particular cases in the
cause list can also be
searched.
Page no 25 e-Courts Services Mobile App

10.My Cases option:
My cases option is one of the most attractive
and useful options for Advocates and Litigants
because it acts as a Digital personal case diary.
It is an exclusive feature available in the e-Courts
App. The Litigant or Lawyer can save and store
his/her cases under My Cases and see the
details as and when required.
10.1. How to add cases to My cases:
If you want to add cases to “My Cases” list then
follow these steps
Step 1: Search the Case which you want to add
to My cases using the e-Courts mobile App.
Step 2: The “add cases” button will be displayed
on the top right-hand side in the Case history of
the searched Case, as shown in the screenshot
herewith.
Step 3: Click the “Add cases “which will add the case to your “My Cases list.”
An advocate or an advocate clerk can add all their office cases in My Cases and
maintain a digital diary of their office case and get updates and status of the
cases using My Cases option. A senior Advocate can add the important cases
alone and keep track of the case status without the help of a junior or an
advocate clerk and can see the case status 24*7. A litigant can also add his cases
under My cases. Likewise, prosecutors, court police constable, Investigating
officers, Government pleaders also can use this "My cases "list and can keep track
of them 24*7
Page no 26 e-Courts Services Mobile App

10.2.How to remove Cases from My Cases:
To remove the cases from "My Cases" one
should open the cases through My Cases,
then that case will display the "Remove
Case" option on the right-hand side top as
shown in the screenshot. If the “Remove
case” option is clicked, it will remove the
case from the My cases list.

11.2. Import option:
The import option is the most
sought after feature by the e-
Courts mobile app user. What to
do if you are going to change your
phone? or when your phone data
gets crashed. Then this import
option is beneficial. You can use
this import option and get the
backup data into your new phone.
When the data is mistakenly
deleted from the phone, one can
use this import option and get the
data restored.
You can click the import icon and
import the data from two options;
(i) Import from drive and
(ii) Import from this device.
The screenshots appended
herewith showing the two options
under "Import from". It is advisable
that at least once you import the
backup data from google drive,
google drive will ask permission, and you can click allow the button to import the
data. The said screenshot is also enclosed herewith. Once the import option is
completed, you will get the alert message 'Cases imported successfully'. Thus, you
can use the import option and get the backup data in your new mobile phone or
restore the backup data from your old mobile phone.
Page no 31 e-Courts Services Mobile App

12.Getting case status using QR Code:
While using the e-Courts Services mobile App, some may find it difficult in typing the
Case Number Record (CNR) number every time for getting the case status or
typing the case details every time you want to get the case updates. There is
another easy way of getting the case details using the QR code scan option in the
e-Courts mobile.
12.1. Step: 1- Getting the QR Code of Your Case:
Get the QR code for your case under the case History from the e-Courts Services
mobile applications. (OR) Get the QR code for your case under the Case History
from the e-Courts services website https://e c ourts.gov.in also.
12.2. Step 2- Take a print out of the QR code and Paste it on the case Docket:
One can take the print out of the QR code and paste it in the case files.
12.3. Step 3-Scan QR Code:
Using the "Scan QR code" option inbuilt in the e-Courts mobile app one can scan
the QR code pasted on the case docket which will immediately show the case
status. This QR Code scanning can be beneficial for advocate office and
Page no 32 e-Courts Services Mobile App

companies/ govt institution having many cases. They can print out the QR Code
and paste it in their case files and scan with their mobile App – Scan QR code
option and get the case details instantly without filing all the points one by one.
13. Get case status through SMS where there is no Internet:
In our country, more than 50% percent of
our people don’t have access to the
internet. As reiterated by the Chairman of
e-Committee we need to have inclusive
system breaking the technological divide
and this service is one such feature which
caters to the need of the people who
don’t have access to the internet. When
you don’t have an internet connection then, you can get the case status by
sending SMS to “ECOURTS<SPACE>< YOUR CNR NUMBER>” to 9766899899.
14. Getting case status through e-Courts Automated email services:
Though the service of automated email services is out of context for the e-Courts
mobile App even then, it is a related feature which can be accessed in your
mobile phone if you are in the practice of checking emails with your mobile phone.
To activate this attractive automated email service, the litigants and the
advocates have to get their email
registered in the concerned Court. The
registered users will get case updates,
next hearing dates, copies of orders and
Judgments and Cause list. An advocate
practicing in Tamil Nadu at Avinashi Sub
Court came one day and happily
shared her excitement and surprise of
receiving her first automated email
regarding the listing of the Case. The
said screenshot is shared herewith for the
readers. A day is not far where one can
Page no 33 e-Courts Services Mobile App

get all the certified copies from the Court at the comfort of the home.
15. Court Complex Locator:
A new option – Court Complex Locator is
added in the e-Court Mobile Application,
which is a handy tool for litigants. If a litigant
receives a summon from far off Courts and is
unaware of the Court's location, he can use
the Court Complex Locator and find the
Court location on the map, and he can
reach the Court using this Court Complex
Locator option. This Court Complex Locator
works on our Indian Mapping App – BHUVAN,
and the screenshots of searching Court at
Coimbatore is shown herewith.
16. Various links in e-Court Mobile App Menu.
Under e-Courts mobile app important links of
e-Courts services are also provided under the
menus options One can access the following
links
e-Pay→
NJDG→
e-Filng→
India Code→
Forms for Advocates→
Virtual courts.→
All these links are available under e-Courts services website. For example if one
wants to pay the online fine, you can directly click the Virtual courts link from the
mobile app and access virtual courts portal and pay the fine without even going
to courts. Hence these links can be used as a real ready reckoners!
Page no 34 e-Courts Services Mobile App

17. e-Pay link in e-Courts Mobile App:
When you click the option e-Pay, it
will take you to the
https://pay.e c ourts.gov.in from where
you can make digital payments for
Court fees, Judicial Deposit, Fine and
Penalty. You can make digital
payments using your CNR number or
case number and by using your
mobile number.
18. NJDG link in the e-Courts mobile app:
When you click the NJDG button, it will take you directly to the NJDG link under
https://njdg.e c ourts.gov.in , from where you can get the following particulars (i) National
Judicial Data Grid (District and Taluka Courts) (ii) National Judicial Data Grid(High
Courts). While using NJDG, you need to select the State, then-District and using the
drill-down option, and you can get a variety of details of the pending cases,
disposed of cases, case type wise, stage-wise, etc. Put your hands on your mobile
to experience the drill-down options !
Page no 35 e-Courts Services Mobile App

19. India Code access through e-Courts Mobile App:
Now a new feature of India Code has
been added to the e-Courts mobile
application. Whereby anyone using it
can get all the Statutes, Acts,
Regulations, Notification, etc. It is a
great ready reckoner of all the bare
Acts in your handset. For example, if you
want to refer to any Section in Civil
Procedure Code, then it can be easily
got from the mobile app link, as shown
herewith..
19.1.Searching Bare Acts from India code
If you want to search any statute, then you have to type the searching code in the
search box, and you can get it from India code. For example, if you want the
Criminal procedure code, or the civil procedure code you can type it in the box
and get it.
Page no 36 e-Courts Services Mobile App

20. e-Filing link in e-Court Mobile App.
You can also access the e-Court services
like e-Filing, e-Payment and NJDG. Once
you click the e-filing application, it will
take you to the e-filing portal
https://efiling.e c ourts.gov.in , and from the
India Map, you can choose your
respective State and start e-filing the
case. You can also access the help
videos and tutorials provided under the e-
filing portal. Start e-filing your cases, and
become a digital era advocate.
21.Virtual Courts link in the e-Courts mobile app:
One can access the virtual Court through the link in the mobile application. The
services offered on the virtual court portal search the cases by mobile number,
CNR, Party Name, search by Challan and Vehicle Number. One can pay his fine
using the mobile application, which leads to the virtual court link. Thus, one can
settle his case by paying the Fine amount in Motor accident cases without going to
Court and logging into the virtual court portal.
Page no 37 e-Courts Services Mobile App

22 Forms for Advocates link in the e-Courts mobile App:
There is a useful link available under
e-Courts mobile application menu -
the Forms for Advocates, the latest
addition. If the said link is clicked, it
will link you to the variety of forms
used by advocates. Example: Bail
Bond, Copy application form (CA
form); case information format, filing
form, index form, Memo of
appearance, Notice to produce
documents, Surety bond,
Vakalatnama bond. Hope it makes you curious enough to check this helpful link.
23.Help option:
How to use the various
options under the e-Court
services has been displayed
under this Help Option
which will come to help
whenever doubt arises.
When you click on every
tab under the help, it will
show the step along with
the help images to use the features. E.g., if you click the tab of My Cases under e-
Courts Services app Help, it will open up the help details as shown in the screenshot
which you can follow and start using the menus.

NSTEP User Manual
2 | P a g e
1. Introduction
National Service and Tracking of Electronic Processes (NSTEP) is an Android OS APP developed
for service and delivery of Court Processes . This App will be used by Bailiffs of the Courts for
delivery of processes. CIS (Case Information System) software is deployed across all Courts in
India. CIS provides facility to generate electronic processes in PDF format. Once the electronic
processes are generated, process admin of the respective court will assign the delivery of
processes to Bailiffs.
To view list of processes allocated to him, Bailiff must have Smartphone with NSTEP App
installed. The Procedure to operate the App is as follows:
1. Bailiff needs to select State from dropdown list and enter Registered Mobile number
and already provided OTP password to login into the system.
Figure 1 : Login
2. Once logged into the system , Main screen of the App will be displayed.
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
3 | P a g e
The Main screen will show following elements
a) On the Top, App will display count of processes for which status needs to be
uploaded on the server.
b) ‘Scan QR Code’ button is used to Scan QR Code of the case and displays list of
processes belonging to that case.
c) Once QR Code is scanned, button ‘Show Previous’ will be enabled. After clicking, it
will show all processes allocated to the Bailiff.
d) List of processes to be served is displayed .
e) ‘Refresh Processes’ button is used to receive newly allocated process to the Bailiff.
Figure 2 :List of Processes
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
4 | P a g e
2. Process Service
1. After the Bailiff reaches the address of the party to whom process is to be served, he
needs to tap on the process from the list which will display the process in PDF format.
Figure 3 : View PDF
2. Hand over the physical copy of the process to the concerned party.
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
5 | P a g e
3. Click on ‘Capture Photo’ to capture photo of the person to whom process is served and
tap on
4. Click on ‘Signature’ to capture the Signature of the person to whom process is served
and tap on
5. Once signature is captured , App displays the map for capturing mobile device location .
Bailiff needs to tap on ‘Save’ button to store Latitude and Longitude of the location.
6. “Reload/Refresh “ floating button is provided to refresh the map.
￼
￼
￼
￼
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
6 | P a g e
Figure 4 : Location
7. After capturing Location details, Bailiff needs to mark the status of process as “Served”
or “Not Served” with respective remarks or reason for serving or non serving.
8. Bailiff needs to tick on ‘Confirm and Upload’ to upload status of process to the server.
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
7 | P a g e
9. While uploading the status of processes to the server if any communication problem
arises or device has network issues, then status gets uploaded locally on the mobile
device of the Bailiff.
10. Bailiff can upload status of processes using ‘UPLOAD’ menu available in Side Menu.
￼
￼
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
8 | P a g e
3. Sidemenu
The Side Menu of App is used for various options like Upload, Delete and Logout.
Figure 5 : Sidemenu
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
9 | P a g e
4. UPLOAD
1. This option displays list of all served processes .
2. Bailiff can upload status of served processes to the server.
3. Re-uploading of process status can also be done from this option.
Figure 6 : Upload
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
10 | P a g e
5. DELETE
1. This option displays list of processes whose status is already uploaded by Bailiff to the server.
2. Delete option is provided to the Bailiff to delete the processes from this list.
Figure 7 : Delete
￼
￼

NSTEP User Manual
11 | P a g e
6. LOGOUT
This option is used to logout from the App.
Figure 8 : Exit
￼

PROJECT BACKGROUND eCourts is a Mission Mode Project which uses technology to
make the judicial processes across over 21000 district and
subordinate courts in India more eﬃcient and speedy.
The project is being implemented under the joint partnership of
Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of
India and eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in a
decentralized manner through the respective High Courts.
Phase-I of the project was approved in 2010 and enabled
computerization of 14,249 district and subordinate courts by
2015 at a cost of Rs. 639 crores.
Phase–II of this project, which envisions further enhancements,
was commissioned in 2015 for a period of four years, at a budget
of Rs 1670 crores.
The focus of the Phase–II is on enhancing judicial service
delivery for litigants and lawyers by improving infrastructure
and providing technology-enabled judicial processes. It involves
improved ICT infrastructure, video conferencing, improved
access across seven platforms including web portal, app, judicial
service centers, kiosks, etc.
The project also includes capacity building of oﬃcers, ICT
provisioning of District Legal Service Authorities, Taluka Legal
Service Committees and State Judicial Academies as well as
judicial process re-engineering.
FOCUS AREAS
• ICT infrastructure, technology-enabled judicial processes and wide
area network connectivity across district and taluka courts
• Delivery of digital court services
through the website, email, mobile app,
SMS, Judicial Service Centers (JSCs), and
touch screen kiosks
• Change management and re-
engineering of the judicial processes
KEY OUTCOMES
eCourts Portal (www.ecourts.gov.in) provides
litigant-centric information.
• Online mechanism for stakeholders such as
litigants, advocates, members of judiciary to
track the court proceedings, status and
judgements
• Portal is disabled
friendly and
responsive
to all devices
• Portal records
more than
1 million hits
National Judicial Data Grid (njdg.ecourts.gov.in)
provides case information statistics:
• Enables transparency in tracking of pendency of
case statistics
• Data from all district & subordinate courts and
from High Courts is available on the grid
• Serves as a national judicial data warehouse that
may be used to drive policy making and decision
support
• Case information software (CIS) version 3.0
implemented in District Courts, version 1.0
implemented in High Courts
eCourts SERVICES
For Litigants and Lawyers:
• Quicker delivery of court services - Case Status
Information, Case Next Date Noti�cations,
Daily Orders / Proceedings, Online Certi�ed
Copies / Judgments, etc
• Easy and eﬃcient access to case information
anytime, anywhere
For Judicial Oﬃcers – an enhanced
case management system that enables:
• Cause list
generation
•
‘On the go’
help menu
• Drill down
calendar
• References to
case laws of High
Courts and
Supreme Court
• Customizable
report generation
with periodic
statistics /
statements
• Video tutorials
and manuals
HIGHLIGHTS OF
eCourts PROJECT
Infrastructure Improvement
• ICT infrastructure covering computer
hardware, Local Area Network(LAN), Wide
Area Network (WAN), information kiosks,
renewable energy, UPS, power backup, etc. in
all district and subordinate courts of the country
• ICT provisioning for District Legal Service
Authorities, Taluka Legal Service Committees
and State Judicial Academies
• Video conferencing facility connecting all
courts and jails - 488 courts and 342 jails
already connected
Platforms for Service Delivery

through these platforms:

to access eCourts
services across
the country
• eCourts Services
mobile application
• SMS pull of case
information by
sending Case
Number Record
(CNR) to +91-97668-99899

automatic case
updates after
registration of
mobile number
• Automated email
noti�cations after
registration
• Information kiosks to
enable self service
• Judicial Service
Centers at court
complexes
Information Kiosk
Unique Features

source software
based project
• QR codes to
enable automatic
case access
• Single uni�ed
portal, across
the country

PROJECT BACKGROUND eCourts is a Mission Mode Project which uses technology to
make the judicial processes across over 21000 district and
subordinate courts in India more eﬃcient and speedy.
The project is being implemented under the joint partnership of
Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of
India and eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in a
decentralized manner through the respective High Courts.
Phase-I of the project was approved in 2010 and enabled
computerization of 14,249 district and subordinate courts by
2015 at a cost of Rs. 639 crores.
Phase–II of this project, which envisions further enhancements,
was commissioned in 2015 for a period of four years, at a budget
of Rs 1670 crores.
The focus of the Phase–II is on enhancing judicial service
delivery for litigants and lawyers by improving infrastructure
and providing technology-enabled judicial processes. It involves
improved ICT infrastructure, video conferencing, improved
access across seven platforms including web portal, app, judicial
service centers, kiosks, etc.
The project also includes capacity building of oﬃcers, ICT
provisioning of District Legal Service Authorities, Taluka Legal
Service Committees and State Judicial Academies as well as
judicial process re-engineering.
FOCUS AREAS
• ICT infrastructure, technology-enabled judicial processes and wide
area network connectivity across district and taluka courts
• Delivery of digital court services
through the website, email, mobile app,
SMS, Judicial Service Centers (JSCs), and
touch screen kiosks
• Change management and re-
engineering of the judicial processes

# National Informatics Centre: Case Information System (CIS): Registration Module & Caveats
Source: e-Committee Supreme Court of India

National Informatics Centre Registration User Manual eCourts Project
1. Introduction
National Informatics Centre Software Development Unit (NIC SDU), Pune, has been entrusted
with the task of software development of Case Information System (CIS) for the country. The
eCourtIS is an eCourt Information System, which is currently implemented in Establishments
(City Courts and Taluka Courts) across India. The application is completely based on Open
Source Technology.
1.1. Scope
The scope of this document is to provide a user manual for the Registration User to operate the
Registration module.
1.1.1. Audience
The target audience for this document is the Registration User. This manual will guide the
Registration User to use Registration module for the Case Registration process.
1.1.2. Purpose of this Document
This document will guide the Registration User to do Case Registration, add Fees, Change
password through User Management menu and view reports in Master menu.
1.1.3. Objective of this Document
The main objective of this document is to enable the Registration User to perform the
following:
• View the reports in the Master menu.
• In Caveat Section menu, do Caveat Registration, Caveat Auto Deletion, Search Caveat,
Caveat Register, and Search Caveat and Tag.
• In Fees menu, add the amount of Fees and select the Fees Type for a Case and view the
Query for the selected Case Type using Case Number, Filing Number, or Caveat Number
of the selected case type.
• In Case Registration menu, do Case Scrutiny, Case Rejection, Case Registration, Urgent
Case, Case Extra Info, IA on Filing, Suit Schedule, Registration Process, and FIR Search.
• In Case Allocation menu, view the Pending Allocation List. The Pending Allocation List
submenu includes the Pending Allocation List and the Institution Register.
• In Litigant Updations menu, you can upload the photo of the Litigant in Photo Upload
sub menu, add Extra Advocate, Legal Heir, Guardian or Attorney Info, and enter the
Litigant Status.
• In User Menu, you can change the password of the Registration user.

Judicial Appointments Procedure, Collegium System & District Judiciary

## Constitutional Framework

  "supreme_court_appointments": "Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India",
  "high_court_appointments": "Article 217(1) of the Constitution of India",
  "high_court_transfers": "Article 222(1) of the Constitution of India",
  "additional_acting_judges": "Article 224 of the Constitution of India",
  "district_judges_appointments": "Article 233 of the Constitution of India (Appointed by State Governor in consultation with High Court)"
}

## Memorandum Of Procedure Mop
{
  "supreme_court_procedure": {
    "source_document": "mop_supreme_court_appointment_of_judges.pdf",
    "initiator": "Chief Justice of India (CJI)",
    "collegium_composition": "CJI and 4 senior-most puisne Judges of the Supreme Court",
    "steps": [
      "CJI initiates recommendation in consultation with 4 senior-most judges of Supreme Court",
      "Consultation with consultee judges (Supreme Court judges conversant with the High Court from which candidate is drawn)",
      "Views of the consultee judges are recorded in writing and form part of the file",
      "CJI forwards agreed recommendation to Union Minister of Law and Justice",
      "Union Law Minister forwards file to Prime Minister after Intelligence Bureau background check",
      "Prime Minister advises President of India",
      "President signs Warrant of Appointment under hand and seal",
      "Official Gazette Notification issued by Department of Justice"
    ]
  },
  "high_court_procedure": {
    "source_document": "mop_high_court_appointment_of_judges.pdf",
    "initiator": "Chief Justice of the High Court",
    "collegium_composition": "Chief Justice of High Court and 2 senior-most puisne Judges of the High Court",
    "timelines": "Proposals must be initiated at least 6 months prior to an anticipated vacancy",
    "recruitment_sources": {
      "bar_advocates": "Approximately two-thirds (66.6%) of vacancies filled from practicing advocates (minimum 10 years practice, typically age 45-55)",
      "judicial_officers": "Approximately one-third (33.3%) of vacancies filled from State Higher Judicial Service (minimum 10 years judicial service)"
    },
    "steps": [
      "High Court Chief Justice consults 2 senior-most puisne judges",
      "Chief Justice sends recommendation to State Governor (who consults Chief Minister)",
      "State Government forwards comments to Union Law Minister within 6 weeks",
      "Union Law Minister conducts background checks via Intelligence Bureau",
      "File submitted to Chief Justice of India",
      "Supreme Court Collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most SC judges + consultee judges) evaluates proposal",
      "SCC conveys concurrence or advice to Union Law Minister",
      "If government has objections, it may return recommendation for reconsideration once",
      "If SCC reiterates recommendation unanimously, appointment is finalized by President"
    ]
  }
}

    "initiator": "Chief Justice of India (CJI)",
    "collegium_composition": "CJI and 4 senior-most puisne Judges of the Supreme Court",
    "steps": [
      "CJI initiates recommendation in consultation with 4 senior-most judges of Supreme Court",
      "Consultation with consultee judges (Supreme Court judges conversant with the High Court from which candidate is drawn)",
      "Views of the consultee judges are recorded in writing and form part of the file",
      "CJI forwards agreed recommendation to Union Minister of Law and Justice",
      "Union Law Minister forwards file to Prime Minister after Intelligence Bureau background check",
      "Prime Minister advises President of India",
      "President signs Warrant of Appointment under hand and seal",
      "Official Gazette Notification issued by Department of Justice"
    ]
  },
  "high_court_procedure": {
    "source_document": "mop_high_court_appointment_of_judges.pdf",
    "initiator": "Chief Justice of the High Court",
    "collegium_composition": "Chief Justice of High Court and 2 senior-most puisne Judges of the High Court",
    "timelines": "Proposals must be initiated at least 6 months prior to an anticipated vacancy",
    "recruitment_sources": {
      "bar_advocates": "Approximately two-thirds (66.6%) of vacancies filled from practicing advocates (minimum 10 years practice, typically age 45-55)",
      "judicial_officers": "Approximately one-third (33.3%) of vacancies filled from State Higher Judicial Service (minimum 10 years judicial service)"
    },
    "steps": [
      "High Court Chief Justice consults 2 senior-most puisne judges",
      "Chief Justice sends recommendation to State Governor (who consults Chief Minister)",
      "State Government forwards comments to Union Law Minister within 6 weeks",
      "Union Law Minister conducts background checks via Intelligence Bureau",
      "File submitted to Chief Justice of India",
      "Supreme Court Collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most SC judges + consultee judges) evaluates proposal",
      "SCC conveys concurrence or advice to Union Law Minister",
      "If government has objections, it may return recommendation for reconsideration once",
      "If SCC reiterates recommendation unanimously, appointment is finalized by President"
    ]
  }
}

## District And Subordinate Judiciary
{
  "sanctioned_strength": "Approximately 25,246 judges (as reported across States/UTs to Supreme Court)",
  "working_strength": "Approximately 19,858 judges",
  "vacancies": "Approximately 5,388 vacancies (~21% vacancy rate)",
  "appointment_authority": "State Governments in consultation with respective High Courts / State Public Service Commissions",
  "recruitment_streams": [
    "Civil Judge (Junior Division): Direct recruitment via State Judicial Services Examination conducted by High Court / State PSC for law graduates",
    "District Judge (Cadre): 65% by promotion based on merit-cum-seniority from Civil Judge (Senior Division); 10% by limited competitive examination; 25% by direct recruitment from Bar (advocates with minimum 7 years practice)"
  ],
  "data_reference_date": "July 2023 (Monsoon Session, Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha parliamentary replies)",
  "source": "Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India (Parliamentary Records & DoJ Monsoon 2023 Compendium)",
  "audit_note": "Historical parliamentary benchmark figures. Distinct from the August 2026 higher judiciary vacancy statements. District judiciary recruitment is continuously administered by respective High Courts and State PSCs under Articles 233/234."
}

# Official Knowledge Guide: Doj Overview And Divisions

## Department
Department of Justice

## Ministry
Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of India

## Official Portal
https://doj.gov.in

## Nodal Responsibilities
{
  "allocation_of_business_rules": "Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961",
  "mandate": [
    "Appointment, resignation, and removal of Chief Justice of India and Judges of the Supreme Court of India",
    "Appointment, resignation, and removal of Chief Justices and Judges of High Courts",
    "Service conditions, salaries, allowances, leave, and pensions of Supreme Court and High Court Judges",
    "Formulation and implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes for the development of infrastructure facilities for the Judiciary (Nyaya Vikas)",
    "Administration of the eCourts Mission Mode Project for computerization and digital transformation of District and Subordinate Courts",
    "Access to Justice and Legal Aid to the poor under the DISHA scheme (Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, Nyaya Mitra, Legal Literacy)",
    "Establishment and monitoring of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) under the Nirbhaya Fund for rape and POCSO Act cases",
    "Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms through the National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms",
    "Administration of the Notaries Act, 1952 and appointment of central notaries",
    "Serving as the nodal agency for the 'Enforcing Contracts' indicator under Ease of Doing Business"
  ]
}

## Leadership And Officials
{
  "minister": "Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ministry of Law and Justice",
  "secretary": "Secretary (Justice), Department of Justice",
  "headquarters": "Jaisalmer House, 26, Mansingh Road, New Delhi - 110011"
}

## Functional Divisions
[
  {
    "name": "Appointments Division (Judicial-I and Judicial-II)",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Processing proposals for appointment of Chief Justice of India and Judges of the Supreme Court",
      "Processing proposals for appointment of Chief Justices and Judges of High Courts in coordination with the Supreme Court Collegium, State Governors, and Prime Minister's Office",
      "Processing transfers of High Court Judges under Article 222 of the Constitution",
      "Managing sanctioned strength, working strength, and vacancies across Supreme Court and all 25 High Courts",
      "Handling post-retirement service conditions and benefits of higher judiciary judges"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "Judicial Infrastructure Division (JR Division)",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Administration of Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Subordinate Judiciary",
      "Fund allocation and monitoring for construction of court buildings and residential quarters for judicial officers",
      "Implementation and monitoring via the 'Nyaya Vikas' web portal and mobile app using geo-tagging and space technology (ISRO NRSC collaboration)",
      "Monitoring state-wise fund utilization and physical progress of infrastructure projects"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "e-Courts Division",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Planning, funding, and monitoring the eCourts Mission Mode Project in coordination with the e-Committee, Supreme Court of India and NIC",
      "Phase I: Computerization of 14,249 district/taluka court complexes",
      "Phase II: Implementation of cloud infrastructure, video conferencing, CIS 3.0, NJDG, eFiling, ePay, and Virtual Courts",
      "Phase III: Approved by Union Cabinet with financial outlay of ₹7,210 crore to create a unified, digital, paperless, AI-enabled court ecosystem"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "Access to Justice (A2J) / DISHA Division",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Implementation of the composite umbrella scheme DISHA (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) for 2021-2026",
      "Tele-Law: Mainstreaming legal aid through Village-Level Common Services Centers (CSCs) and Tele-Law Mobile App",
      "Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services): Connecting registered practicing advocates with underprivileged litigants through mobile app",
      "Nyaya Mitra: Assisting District Judiciary in reducing pendency of cases older than 10 years by facilitating litigants",
      "Pan-India Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness programs"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) Division",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Centrally Sponsored Scheme under Nirbhaya Fund launched in October 2019 for expeditious disposal of Rape and POCSO Act cases",
      "Coordination with 30 States/UTs and High Courts for operationalization of 782+ FTSCs including 413+ exclusive POCSO courts",
      "Cabinet approval of scheme extension up to 31st March 2026 with total outlay of ₹1,952.23 crore (Central share: ₹1,207.24 crore from Nirbhaya Fund)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Formulated to ensure phased reduction of arrears and backlog in courts",
      "Commissioning Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms through leading academic institutions, NLUs, and think tanks",
      "Promoting alternative dispute resolution (ADR), commercial dispute resolution, and mediation framework"
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "Notary Cell",
    "responsibilities": [
      "Administration of the Notaries Act, 1952 and Notaries Rules, 1956",
      "Conducting online examinations / interviews and issuing certificates of practice for Central Notaries across India"
    ]
  }
]

## Major Flagship Schemes
[
  {
    "scheme_name": "eCourts Mission Mode Project",
    "nature": "Central Sector Scheme / National e-Governance Project",
    "financial_allocation_phase_3": "₹7,210 Crore",
    "objectives": "Paperless digital courts, digitizing legacy records, AI-assisted transcription and translation, cloud computing, intelligent case management"
  },
  {
    "scheme_name": "CSS for Subordinate Judiciary Infrastructure (Nyaya Vikas)",
    "nature": "Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)",
    "sharing_pattern": "60:40 for general states, 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, 100% for UTs",
    "portal": "https://nyayavikas.gov.in"
  },
  {
    "scheme_name": "DISHA (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice)",
    "nature": "Central Sector Scheme (2021-2026)",
    "components": [
      "Tele-Law",
      "Nyaya Bandhu",
      "Nyaya Mitra",
      "Legal Literacy and Awareness"
    ]
  },
  {
    "scheme_name": "Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)",
    "nature": "Centrally Sponsored Scheme under Nirbhaya Fund",
    "duration": "Extended through 31st March 2026",
    "financial_outlay": "₹1,952.23 Crore"
  }
]

# Official Knowledge Guide: Ecourts Mobile App Guide

## Topic
eCourts Services Mobile Application

## App Name
eCourts Services

## Developer
National Informatics Centre (NIC) for e-Committee, Supreme Court of India

## Download Links
{
  "android_google_play": "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.ecourts.eCourtsServices",
  "ios_apple_app_store": "https://apps.apple.com/in/app/ecourts-services/id1260905877"
}

## Awards
Digital India Award - Platinum Category (Excellence in Digital Governance)

## Downloads And Usage
Over 5.8+ million downloads across India; operational 24x7 for citizens, advocates, judiciary, police, and government departments

## Supported Languages
[
  "English",
  "Hindi",
  "Assamese",
  "Bengali",
  "Gujarati",
  "Kannada",
  "Khasi",
  "Malayalam",
  "Marathi",
  "Nepali",
  "Odia",
  "Punjabi",
  "Tamil",
  "Telugu"
]

## Core Features
{
  "cnr_search": {
    "description": "Primary search parameter using the unique 16-character alphanumeric Case Natural Record number",
    "function": "Instantly displays case details, current status, previous and next hearing dates, court number, and judge designation"
  },
  "case_status_search_options": [
    "Case Number (Case Type, Number, Year)",
    "FIR Number (Police Station, FIR number, Year)",
    "Party Name (Petitioner / Respondent)",
    "Advocate Name / Bar Council Enrollment Number",
    "Filing Number",
    "Act and Section (e.g., Sec 138 NI Act, Sec 302 IPC)",
    "Caveat Search"
  ],
  "cause_list": {
    "description": "Daily cause list of District Courts, Taluka Courts, and High Courts",
    "filtering": "Can be filtered by Court Complex, Judge / Court Room number, Advocate name, or Date of hearing"
  },
  "my_cases_portfolio": {
    "description": "Personalized digital case tracker for advocates and litigants",
    "functionality": [
      "Add cases to 'My Cases' portfolio by clicking the 'Add to Portfolio' bookmark icon",
      "Group cases into customizable folders (e.g., Client-wise, Court-wise, Urgent)",
      "Automatic push notifications and alerts whenever a new order is uploaded, next date is assigned, or case status changes",
      "Backup and restore portfolio to local device or cloud drive"
    ]
  },
  "qr_code_scanner": {
    "description": "Built-in QR code reader within the mobile app",
    "usage": "Litigants and advocates can scan the QR code printed on case acknowledgments, certified copies, or eCourts web pages to immediately open the live case profile on their phone"
  },
  "orders_and_judgments": {
    "description": "In-app viewer and direct download of interim daily orders, proceeding sheets, and final judgments in PDF format"
  },
  "calendar_view": {
    "description": "Visual judicial diary displaying hearing schedules, holidays, and listed cases in a calendar grid"
  }
}

# Official Knowledge Guide: Efiling Complete Process Guide

## Topic
eFiling System for High Courts and District Courts

## Portal Url
https://filing.ecourts.gov.in

## Version
eFiling 3.0 / eFiling 2.0

## Source Documents
[
  "efiling_user_manual_ecourts.pdf (eCommittee Supreme Court of India)",
  "case_filing_user_manual.pdf",
  "efiling_registration_user_manual.pdf",
  "model_rules_for_efiling_supreme_court_ecommittee.pdf"
]

## Registration Process
{
  "advocate_registration": {
    "steps": [
      "Visit https://filing.ecourts.gov.in",
      "Select State and High Court or District Court",
      "Select User Type: Advocate",
      "Enter Bar Council Enrollment Number (e.g., D/1234/2015)",
      "Enter registered mobile number and email ID",
      "Validate through OTP received on mobile and email",
      "Create secure Password and upload Identity proof (Bar Council ID)",
      "Approval by Court Administration / Registry admin",
      "Activation SMS and email confirmation received"
    ]
  },
  "litigant_in_person_registration": {
    "steps": [
      "Select User Type: Party-in-Person / Litigant",
      "Enter Official Identity / Aadhaar verification",
      "Provide mobile number, email address, residential address",
      "Verify through OTP",
      "Submit registration request for verification"
    ]
  }
}

## Document Preparation Standards
{
  "file_format": "PDF/A or Searchable PDF with Optical Character Recognition (OCR)",
  "scan_resolution": "200 to 300 DPI in black and white or grayscale",
  "file_size_limit": "Typically up to 50 MB per file (split into volumes if larger)",
  "digital_signature": "Digital Signature Certificate (DSC Class 3 token) or Aadhaar-based eSign",
  "page_indexing_and_bookmarking": "Mandatory electronic index with hyperlinks / bookmarks to annexures and exhibits"
}

## Filing Workflow Steps
[
  "1. Login to eFiling Portal using registered credentials and OTP",
  "2. Select Court Complex and Case Type (Civil, Criminal, Writ, Appeal, etc.)",
  "3. Enter Petitioner / Complainant details (Name, Age, Gender, Address, Mobile, Email)",
  "4. Enter Respondent / Accused details",
  "5. Add Extra Parties (Co-petitioners, Co-respondents)",
  "6. Enter Acts and Sections under which case is filed",
  "7. Enter Subordinate Court details (Lower court case number, trial judge, order date if filing Appeal/Revision)",
  "8. Upload Petition, Affidavits, Vakalatnama, Impugned Order, and Annexures",
  "9. Digitally sign documents using DSC or eSign",
  "10. Calculate and pay Court Fee via integrated ePay gateway (or enter e-Challan details)",
  "11. Complete Verification / Affirmation statement",
  "12. Generate OTP to finalize submission",
  "13. System generates temporary eFiling Acknowledgment Number",
  "14. Scrutiny by Court Registry (Defects / Objections notified online via SMS/Email)",
  "15. Cure of Defects by Advocate within prescribed time window (re-upload corrected files)",
  "16. Acceptance by Registry and generation of regular Court Case Number and unique 16-character CNR Number"
]

  "4. Enter Respondent / Accused details",
  "5. Add Extra Parties (Co-petitioners, Co-respondents)",
  "6. Enter Acts and Sections under which case is filed",
  "7. Enter Subordinate Court details (Lower court case number, trial judge, order date if filing Appeal/Revision)",
  "8. Upload Petition, Affidavits, Vakalatnama, Impugned Order, and Annexures",
  "9. Digitally sign documents using DSC or eSign",
  "10. Calculate and pay Court Fee via integrated ePay gateway (or enter e-Challan details)",
  "11. Complete Verification / Affirmation statement",
  "12. Generate OTP to finalize submission",
  "13. System generates temporary eFiling Acknowledgment Number",
  "14. Scrutiny by Court Registry (Defects / Objections notified online via SMS/Email)",
  "15. Cure of Defects by Advocate within prescribed time window (re-upload corrected files)",
  "16. Acceptance by Registry and generation of regular Court Case Number and unique 16-character CNR Number"
]

# Official Knowledge Guide: Epay Complete Process Guide

## Topic
ePay - Online Court Fee Payment System

## Portal Url
https://pay.ecourts.gov.in

## Source Documents
[
  "epay_final_user_manual.pdf (eCourts Services)",
  "epay_brochure_ecommittee.pdf (eCommittee Supreme Court)"
]

## Payment Categories
[
  {
    "name": "Court Fee",
    "description": "Court fee payable on petitions, plaints, applications, and appeals"
  },
  {
    "name": "Judicial Deposit",
    "description": "Amounts deposited under court orders, maintenance, rent control, compensation"
  },
  {
    "name": "Fine",
    "description": "Fines imposed in criminal proceedings or traffic challans"
  },
  {
    "name": "Penalty / Other Fees",
    "description": "Late filing penalties, certified copy inspection charges, process fees"
  }
]

## Workflows
{
  "new_case_payment": [
    "1. Visit https://pay.ecourts.gov.in",
    "2. Select State, District, and Court Establishment",
    "3. Select 'New Case'",
    "4. Enter Party Name (Petitioner / Complainant)",
    "5. Enter Mobile Number and Email ID",
    "6. Enter Court Fee Amount",
    "7. Select Payment Gateway (SBI ePay / State Treasury / e-GRAS)",
    "8. Complete online banking / UPI / card transaction",
    "9. Generate and download official e-Payment Receipt with Challan Reference ID"
  ],
  "existing_case_payment": [
    "1. Select 'Existing Case'",
    "2. Search case by 16-character CNR Number or Case Number / Filing Number",
    "3. Confirm case and party details displayed on screen",
    "4. Enter Fee Head (Court fee, Process fee, Fine)",
    "5. Enter payment amount and proceed to checkout",
    "6. Download payment acknowledgment"
  ]
}

## Transaction Verification And Security
{
  "receipt_verification": "Can be re-downloaded anytime from portal using Transaction ID or Challan Number",
  "defacement_mechanism": "Once e-Receipt is submitted to court during filing, registry electronically consumes/locks the challan in the CIS system to prevent reuse or fraudulent multi-filing",
  "refund_procedure": "Court fees once paid are non-refundable online directly through ePay. Litigants must file a formal refund application before the concerned Presiding Judge under Section 13/14 of the Court Fees Act, 1870. If granted, the court issues a judicial refund certificate directed to the State Collector/Treasury."
}

chunks.topic: Tele-Law
chunks.source_content:
# Official Knowledge Guide: Tele Law Complete Guide

## Topic
Tele-Law: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized

## Portals
[
  {
    "name": "Tele-Law Official Portal",
    "url": "https://www.tele-law.in",
    "faq_url": "https://www.tele-law.in/faq.html"
  }
]

## Governing Scheme
DISHA (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) by Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, in partnership with National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and CSC e-Governance Services India Limited

## Objective
Connecting marginalized, vulnerable, and rural citizens with panel lawyers through Video Conferencing and telecommunication facilities available at Common Services Centers (CSCs) and via the Tele-Law Citizen Mobile Application.

## Statutory Eligibility Criteria
{
  "legal_basis": "Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987",
  "eligible_categories_for_free_legal_aid": [
    "Women and Children",
    "Members of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)",
    "Victims of trafficking in human beings or begar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution",
    "Persons with disabilities (mental or physical disability)",
    "Victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake, or industrial disaster",
    "Industrial workmen",
    "Persons in custody, including custody in a protective home or psychiatric hospital/nursing home",
    "Persons whose annual income does not exceed the ceiling limit prescribed by the respective State Government (typically up to ₹3,00,000 per annum in most states)"
  ],
  "fee_structure": "Free of cost consultation for all eligible beneficiaries under Section 12 of Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Advice is made available freely across the country."
}

## Access Channels
{
  "csc_channel": {
    "facility": "Gram Panchayat Level Common Services Centers (CSCs)",
    "facilitators": "Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) and Para-Legal Volunteers (PLVs)",
    "workflow": [
      "Citizen visits local CSC kiosk in their village or town",
      "VLE logs into Tele-Law portal and registers citizen's name, gender, contact number, category, and case summary",
      "Relevant documents (revenue records, police complaints, notices) are scanned and uploaded",
      "VLE books an appointment slot with a Panel Lawyer on the portal calendar",
      "SMS confirmation with date, time, and lawyer details is sent to citizen's mobile",
      "On appointment date, citizen joins video call / audio call with the Panel Lawyer at the CSC kiosk",
      "Panel Lawyer gives legal advice, writes written advice/recommendation on the portal, and advises on next legal steps",
      "If case requires court litigation representation, matter is forwarded to District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for assigning a free legal aid advocate"
    ]
  },
  "citizen_mobile_app_channel": {
    "app_name": "Tele-Law Citizen App",
    "availability": "Google Play Store (Android) and Apple App Store (iOS)",
    "languages": "Available in 22 official Indian languages",
    "features": [
      "Direct self-registration by citizen using OTP authentication",
      "Selecting nature of dispute (Family/Matrimonial, Property/Land disputes, Dowry/Domestic Violence, Labour issues, Consumer rights, Criminal matters)",
      "Direct appointment booking with lawyer without visiting CSC",
      "Video / Voice call consultation directly from smartphone",
      "Access to digital copy of lawyer's written advice"
    ]
  }
}

## Panel Lawyers Network
{
  "empanelment": "Panel Lawyers are empanelled by State Legal Services Authorities (SLSA) and District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA) in coordination with Department of Justice",
  "expertise": "Trained legal professionals proficient in local languages, constitutional law, criminal law, civil/property matters, and welfare entitlements"
}
